question: When two-way traffic must share one lane for a limited distance, what coordination rule and control methods apply?
model_answer: Direct Answer: When traffic in both directions must use a single lane for a limited distance, movements from each end of the section are required to be coordinated. Alternating one-way movement should be provided by methods such as flagger control, flag transfer, a pilot car, traffic control signals, or stop or yield control. If traffic control signals are used, they must include adequate red clearance intervals and a means (such as interconnection) to prevent conflicting green indications at opposite ends. Standards (mandatory): - "Except as provided in Paragraph 4 of this Section, when traffic in both directions must use a single lane for a limited distance, movements from each end shall be coordinated." - If signals are used: "The provisions of Chapters 4D through 4G shall apply to traffic control signals for one-lane, two-way facilities, except that: A. The durations of the red clearance intervals shall be adequate to clear the one-lane section of conflicting vehicles; and B. Adequate means, such as interconnection, shall be provided to prevent conflicting signal indications, such as green and green, at opposite ends of the section." Guidance (recommended): - "Provisions should be made for alternate one-way movement through the constricted section via methods such as flagger control, a flag transfer, a pilot car, traffic control signals, or stop or yield control." Citations: - Section 6E.01 Standard §1 (p.787) - Section 6E.01 Guidance §2 (p.787) - Section 4O.02 Standard §1 (p.744)
gold_answer: Movements from both ends must be coordinated, except for a short, low-volume, mutually visible work zone that can self-regulate. Methods include flaggers, flag transfer, a pilot car, temporary traffic signals, or stop/yield control.
